Repair Tier-1 CAS filename/content hash mismatches ("CAS file corruption detected").

Input format: TSV with columns:
  object_kind <tab> object_id <tab> file_path <tab> message

This command:
  - Writes a correctly named content-hash file alongside the corrupt file
  - Updates the CAS index mapping (ID -> content hash) under cross-process lock
  - Moves the corrupt file into a quarantine folder for forensic inspection

If the file is already correctly addressed (64-hex filename stem equals SHA-256 of file content), repair is a no-op
(no quarantine; avoids deleting the only blob when re-running repair after content was fixed).

Examples:
  # Dry run from the latest system-health report
  zqk system repair-cas-corruption --input-file .zqk/system-health/tier1-cas-corruption.tsv --dry-run

  # Apply repairs (recommended to stop scheduler while repairing scheduler_job objects)
  zqk system repair-cas-corruption --input-file .zqk/system-health/tier1-cas-corruption.tsv

Usage:
  zqk system repair-cas-corruption [flags]

Flags:
      --dry-run                 Show what would be repaired without making changes
      --input-file string       Path to TSV input file (defaults to .zqk/system-health/tier1-cas-corruption.tsv)
      --quarantine-dir string   Directory to move corrupt files into (defaults to .zqk/system-health/quarantine)
      --restart-scheduler       Restart scheduler daemon after repair (only if --stop-scheduler is true)
      --stop-scheduler          Stop scheduler daemon before repairing (recommended for scheduler_job corruption)

Global Flags:
      --allow-degraded   Allow scheduler-dependent commands to run when scheduler daemon is not running
